Subject: Retention / redaction questions — PII (SSN / acct numbers)

Camila — thanks for the demo last week. As we pull together risk and compliance for the evaluation, Legal and InfoSec asked for a few specific answers around PII retention and redaction: 

1) Can Redwood enforce per-tenant retention windows for raw PII (SSN, bank acct numbers)? We need the ability to set retention floors and ceilings by tenant/region and trigger on-demand erasure.

2) What redaction options are available at ingestion vs at-serving time? Our compliance team prefers that sensitive identifiers be irreversibly redacted as early as possible, but the product team wants last-4 visibility for fraud triage in a limited window. Can both be supported?

3) Residency: we need a statement on whether retained tokens or cached prompts containing account identifiers can be stored outside the customer’s region.

4) Evidence: will you provide proof of erasure (audit log entries / deletion receipts) and a SOC2 control mapping for the workflow?

Could you send a short write-up or sample configuration (redaction examples) and a proposed next step (technical call with the infra folks)? Legal is on this thread.

Thanks,

Hi Samir — great questions, and totally expected for a regulated payments platform. High-level answers below; attaching a short summary (FI-Retention-Summary.pdf) and a couple of example configs. Happy to schedule a 45-minute call with our infra/security leads to walk through the technical options and compliance evidence.

Summary answers (TL;DR):
- Per-tenant retention: yes — Redwood supports tenant-scoped retention policies. You can set a retention floor (minimum retention driven by business needs) and a maximum retention TTL; policies are enforced by the storage lifecycle and by automatic scrub jobs.
- Redaction modes: three supported patterns: 
  * irreversible tokenization (hashing with tenant-bound salt) at ingestion — irreversible and gold-standard for compliance; best if you never need raw values.
  * reversible pseudonymization (encrypted token vault with access controls) — allows controlled unmasking for authorized workflows with audit logs.
  * selective masking (e.g., show last-4) — can be applied at query-time with role-based gating and ephemeral cache policies.
- Residency & cache: cached prefixes/KV may be stored in the region you select for the deployment (we support region pinning). By default hosted instances store caches and long-term storage in the deployment region; for Dedicated/Private we can ensure all persisted artifacts remain in your VPC/region.
- Proof of erasure & audit: we produce deletion receipts (log entries with job id + timestamp) and can map the workflow to SOC2 control points. We can also provide a limited redaction/audit sample (redaction-examples.json).

Next steps: 1) Technical deep dive with Vivek (serving/runtime) and Marcus (platform/compliance) — propose 11/2 or 11/3; 2) we'll send a short playbook that maps options to risk tradeoffs and costs.

Attachments:
- FI-Retention-Summary.pdf (high-level options + recommended defaults for fintech)
- redaction-examples.json (sample config; see internal notes on key rotation)

Best,

Vivek/Marcus — looping you in for technical detail; Samir asked for concrete guidance on: tenant-scoped retention, irreversible redaction at ingestion vs masking at serve-time, region pinning for caches, and evidence of erasure.

Please see below for what I think we should propose (bullet draft):
1) Per-tenant retention enforcement: implement TTL metadata on stored records; background scrub job deletes objects and writes deletion-records to the audit store with job id + SHA of object. Provide deletion receipts for legal.
2) Ingestion-time irreversible redaction: offer a default pipeline stage that runs deterministic salted-hash per-tenant and drops the original. Note: hashed SSNs are irreversible — we should call this out to Legal.
3) Reversible vault option: for customers that need occasional unmasking (fraud), use an encrypted token vault with KMS-backed keys and RBAC with just-in-time access; unmasking requires an auditable request.
4) Mask-last-4: implement at serving layer with ephemeral KV cache (TTL=72h by default) and role-based gating; logs must show which token was unmasked and by whom.
5) Residency: for Hosted we pin long-term storage to the selected region; caches may be multi-region unless the customer has Dedicated/Private. We should be explicit about which caches may replicate.

Can you (Vivek) confirm feasibility and perf/cost tradeoffs (KV cache TTL, impact on latency for masked/unmasked flows)? Marcus — can you propose the language we should give Legal about deletion receipts and SOC2 mapping? Also attach the sample redaction-examples.json (I attached it in my reply to Samir).

Thanks — want to get this back to Samir by EOD.

Camila

Hi Samir — Marcus from Platform Compliance here. Quick answers and our recommended default for a fintech customer: 

1) Per-tenant retention: supported. Implementation: metadata TTL on objects + periodic secure-delete job. Deletion receipts: for each delete we emit an immutable audit record (timestamp, tenant-id, object-hash, job-id). We can export these receipts (signed) on request for investigations.

2) Redaction modes (tradeoffs):
  - Ingestion irreversible hashing: strongest from a re-identification perspective. Cannot be reversed — recommended when you can tolerate losing the raw value. Low cost.
  - Reversible encrypted tokens (vault): supports controlled unmasking for fraud ops. Requires KMS-backed key management; we log key usage and unmask events for audit. Medium cost.
  - Masking-last-4 at serve-time: preserves some operational utility for support/fraud; implemented at the serving layer with ephemeral cache and RBAC gating. Higher complexity and slightly higher latency when looking up unmasks.

3) Residency: Hosted-by-default stores long-term data in the chosen region and keeps ephemeral caches regionally local where possible. For customers requiring strict residency we recommend Dedicated or Redwood Private (VPC) so we can guarantee no cross-region replication and keep all persisted artifacts in-customer-region.

4) Proof of erasure & SOC2 mapping: we can provide deletion receipts and a control-mapping document that aligns the deletion pipeline with SOC2 CC6.1/CC7.4 (we'll provide the exact mapping in the playbook). We can also provide a sample audit export for your InfoSec team in the technical call.

Recommended default for FinLevel evaluation:
- Start with ingestion-time pseudonymization (reversible tokens) + masking-last-4 at serve time for support flows.
- Configure a 90-day ephemeral cache TTL for any unmask keys; set per-tenant TTLs for raw retention (e.g., 30 days raw + 90-day masked cache), then autodelete.
- Use Dedicated or Private for regionally constrained legal requirements.

I'll attach the sample redaction JSON and a one-page mapping to SOC2 controls after this mail. If that works, Camila can schedule the technical deep dive next week.
